requirements.statement: Define normative terms for agent, tool, capability, task, identity, trust domain, evidence, and lifecycle.
Every normative requirement has a stable ID and explicit verification method.
Architecture decisions identify alternatives, consequences, and supersession.
Validate agent, tool, service, and dataset manifests against a versioned schema.
Manifests declare owner, lifecycle, capabilities, trust domain, scopes, and provenance.
Manifest schema rejects credential material and unknown top-level fields.
Every published schema has a stable identifier and declared version.
Compatibility checks compare schema revisions and representative payload fixtures.
Schema publication records provenance and deprecation policy.
Represent principal identity separately from authorization decisions.
Support credential expiry, rotation, revocation, and trust-domain boundaries.
Reject replayed or unauthenticated requests before protected operation execution.
Generate an SBOM for each releasable software artifact.
Verify release provenance and artifact signatures before promotion.
Pin CI actions and minimize workflow token permissions.
Evaluate principal, action, resource, context, and requested scope as separate policy inputs.
Default-deny when policy is unavailable, malformed, or indeterminate for protected actions.
Record decision identifiers and reasons suitable for audit without exposing secrets.
Record actor, action, target, time, correlation ID, and outcome for security-relevant events.
Distinguish source observation, transformation, and analyst interpretation.
Detect tampering and gaps without treating hashes as proof of factual truth.
